Cautiously positive, with a slight upward tilt after incorporating SLOOS. The FOMC’s taper alongside a 0–0.25% policy rate and AIT keeps conditions accommodative, and the FSR still flags elevated asset valuations, leverage, and nonbank funding risks. However, the latest SLOOS points to broadly improving credit supply and demand: banks eased standards across residential real estate (including HELOCs and jumbo), consumer (credit cards and autos), and CRE (multifamily and nonfarm nonresidential), raised credit card limits and reduced auto-loan rates, and reported stronger or expected stronger demand for consumer and credit card loans and anticipated stronger C&I demand. Foreign banks also eased CRE standards and saw stronger CRE demand, citing improved economic outlook, competition, liquidity, capital positions, and higher risk tolerance. Pockets of softer demand (e.g., some C&I and auto) temper the picture, and the FSR’s vulnerabilities remain relevant. Net: the SLOOS corroborates easy financial conditions and prospective credit growth, nudging sentiment modestly more positive than the FOMC+FSR read alone.
